title: Egg Drop Soup with Ginger and Spring Onion
summary: A light, clear Chinese soup of ginger- and coriander-infused broth, gently thickened and filled with fine, fully set egg ribbons. Spring onions and white pepper give it a fresh, warming finish.
equipment: second saucepan or large heatproof bowl

ingredients.item: spring onions, thinly sliced on an angle

steps.title: Infuse the broth
steps.text: Combine the broth, water, garlic, ginger, coriander sprigs and white peppercorns in the medium saucepan and bring to the boil. Then turn the heat down and let it simmer gently for 20 minutes. Slow simmering draws the aromatic oils out of the ginger and coriander stalks, giving a deeply flavoured broth without clouding it.

steps.title: Strain and season
steps.text: Pour the broth through the sieve into the second pan and discard the solids. Stir in the soy sauce, taste, and add a pinch of salt only if it needs it, then bring back to a simmer. Seasoning after straining lets you judge the true flavour, as the broth reduces slightly while infusing.

steps.title: Thicken lightly
steps.text: In a small bowl, stir 1 tbsp of the cornflour into the cold water until smooth, then whisk it into the simmering broth. Simmer for about 1 minute, until the broth looks a little glossy and slightly thicker. That gentle body helps the egg ribbons stay suspended instead of sinking to the bottom.

steps.title: Pour the egg ribbons
steps.text: Beat the eggs with the remaining 1 tsp cornflour until no streaks remain. Turn the heat down so the soup barely simmers, give it one slow stir, then pour the egg in a thin stream through the tines of a fork. As the egg meets the moving broth it stretches into long, delicate strands; the cornflour in the egg keeps them tender.

steps.title: Let them set
steps.text: Leave the soup undisturbed for 15-20 seconds, until the ribbons are firm and opaque all the way through. Only then stir gently to break them into wisps. Stirring too early smears the egg and clouds the broth, while waiting gives clean, fully cooked ribbons.

steps.title: Serve hot
steps.text: Ladle the soup into bowls and scatter over the spring onions and ground white pepper. Serving straight away keeps the spring onions crisp and the broth at its best.

tips: A common mistake is pouring the eggs into a rapidly boiling soup, which breaks them into tiny grainy bits; keep it barely simmering for long, silky ribbons.
Pour slowly and from a little height for the finest strands.
Always re-stir the cornflour mixture just before adding it, as the starch settles quickly.
Taste before adding any salt, because broth and soy sauce both bring saltiness.
storage: Best served fresh, but leftovers keep covered in the fridge for up to 2 days; freezing is not recommended. Reheat gently on the hob until piping hot (74°C), stirring carefully so the ribbons do not break up too much. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
